questions.question: What type of variation is characterized by features that fall into distinct, limited categories with no intermediates?
options: Continuous variation
Discontinuous variation
Environmental variation
Clinal variation

questions.question: Which statement best describes continuous variation?
options: Features can take any value within a range
Features are limited to distinct, non-overlapping groups
Features are only influenced by a single gene and never by environment
Features are always identical between parents and offspring

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of discontinuous variation in humans?
options: Body mass
ABO blood group
Height
Skin color

questions.question: What is the most appropriate type of chart or graph to display continuous data, such as a range of plant heights?
options: Bar chart
Pie chart
Histogram
Pictogram

questions.question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of continuous variation?
options: It is determined by a single gene and is unaffected by the environment.
It is usually influenced by many factors, including genetics, environment, and lifestyle.
It is only caused by accidental physical injuries.
It divides a population into distinct, non-overlapping categories.

questions.question: When displaying discontinuous data, such as eye color in a classroom, which type of graph should be used?
options: Histogram
Line graph
Bar chart
Scatter graph

questions.question: Why is discontinuous variation, such as whether a person can roll their tongue, unaffected by a person's lifestyle or environment?
options: It has only a genetic cause
It is acquired during a person's lifetime
It is controlled entirely by diet
It changes as a person gets older

questions.question: When a pair of dogs reproduces, they produce puppies rather than kittens. Which concept does this illustrate?
options: Environmental adaptation
Discontinuous variation
Species resemblance
Acquired characteristics

questions.question: Why do offspring typically show a family resemblance, looking similar to their parents and siblings?
options: They live in the exact same location and eat the same food
They inherit features from both parents
They copy the behavior of older family members
They are clones of one of their parents

questions.question: How are inherited features passed from parents to offspring during reproduction?
options: Through the transmission of learned behaviors
By physical contact after birth
Through DNA passed from parents to offspring
Via environmental nutrients in the womb

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a feature changed primarily by an organism's lifestyle and environment?
options: Naturally occurring blood type
The ability to speak a specific language fluently
Having detached earlobes
The natural color of a person's eyes

questions.question: In sexual reproduction, which of the following is true about the offspring?
options: They are always identical clones of the mother.
They are usually identical to their siblings.
There is usually variation between offspring, and they are not identical to their parents.
They always look exactly like the father.

questions.question: How do differences between different species compare to differences within the same species?
options: Differences within a species are much larger than differences between species.
Differences between species are greater than differences within species.
There are no differences between individuals of the same species.
The differences are exactly equal in all cases.

questions.question: What is the term used to describe the differences in features between individuals of the same species?
options: Classification
Variation
Inheritance
Evolution

questions.question: Which of the following variations is caused solely by the environment?
options: Having a scar from an injury
Having blue eyes
Having blood type O
Being biologically male or female

questions.question: Which variation is determined strictly by inherited genetic information in the genome?
options: A tan from sun exposure
The ability to play the piano
A person's ABO blood type
Muscle mass built from weightlifting

questions.question: Why is human body mass considered a product of both genetic and environmental factors?
options: It is decided purely by a single gene at birth and never changes.
It is only affected by the number of hours spent sleeping.
It is influenced by inherited genes as well as diet and exercise lifestyle.
It is an injury-based variation with no biological basis.
